status: Scheduler defect reproduced and patched in a separate executable; full simulator runtime and corner validation pending

patched.effect: Recheck the existing wait deadline against batch-entry time after every VM step; a newly issued positive Wait returns to the controller instead of busy-spinning until budget exhaustion. Physics can update before the next VM batch.

static_evidence.runner_loop: 0x40a455..0x40a4a4: elapsed wall time budget, Interpreter::step, repeat without rechecking entry gate
static_evidence.step_wait_gate: 0x40a544..0x40a55e: GetTickCount compared with deadline; no physics call
static_evidence.clock_import: 0x424078 = KERNEL32 GetTickCount (verified PE import, not SDL_GetTicks)
static_evidence.physics_dt_cap: 0x419fd6..0x419ff5: simulation delta above 0.5 replaced with 0.5; unchanged
static_evidence.motor_speed: 0x410685..0x410693: speed multiplied by 10; ordinary power15 gives150 counts/s absent other motor modes/limits
static_evidence.encoder_integration: 0x4113b1..0x411429: speed * physics delta updates float counters; not advanced by NXC Wait itself

reproduction.method: Unicorn x86 emulation of original/patched runner bytes, deterministic GetTickCount and a stub Interpreter::step implementing the inspected deadline/Wait semantics
reproduction.limitations: VM payload is stubbed; this is not a full RXE, physics, Wine, GUI or end-to-end execution. Large budgets are a controlled counterexample, not measured frame times of historical runs.

geometry_findings: Both-black initial contact does not constrain approach heading to zero; both-gray entry does not uniquely locate axle pose or identify a corner.

A relative quarter-turn preserves entry heading error. Analytical terminal-edge examples with headings -10/0/+10 all give both-gray entry and outgoing headings80/90/100, with differing lateral positions.
These examples use hypothetical symmetric20degree sensors, not measured active angles or a surveyed scene.
Removing60counts changes ideal outgoing lateral position by0.20944sceneunits at zero entry yaw, not outgoing yaw. It cannot generically correct an unknown entry heading.
With C left/A right, left-only exit braking C and advancing A has the correct leftward differential sign. No evidence supports reversing it.
Repeated command resets and inter-command movement make exit349/192 sampled totals insufficient for exact net yaw. Aggregate contact counts also omit ordering.
Exact active sensor mounts, map edge positions, entry yaw, footprint containment and final alignment remain unmeasured. No geometry/power/angle tuning is justified by this audit.
historical_attribution: The scheduler defect can burn sample guards on stale physical readings, but stdout has no frame timing. It is NOT proven to be the cause of C193/C683 or all stalls; dt clamping and other runtime states remain possible contributors.
preservation: Original executable, resources, NXC, RXE, motion powers, angular references and watchdogs unchanged. Existing stdout snapshotted before alternative deployment.
